ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via
Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
Omar Khaab
Stanford University
okhaab@stanford.edu

Stanford University

ABSTRACT
Recent progress in Natural Language Understanding (NLU) is driving fast-paced advances in Information Retrieval (IR), largely owed
to fine-tuning deep language models (LMs) for document ranking.

While remarkably effective, the ranking models based on these LMs
increase computational cost by orders of magnitude over prior approaches, particularly as they must feed each query–document pair
through a massive neural network to compute a single relevance
score.

To tackle this, we present ColBERT, a novel ranking model
that adapts deep LMs (in particular, BERT) for efficient retrieval.

ColBERT introduces a late interaction architecture that independently encodes the query and the document using BERT and then
employs a cheap yet powerful interaction step that models their
fine-grained similarity.

By delaying and yet retaining this finegranular interaction, ColBERT can leverage the expressiveness of
deep LMs while simultaneously gaining the ability to pre-compute
document representations offline, considerably speeding up query
processing.

Beyond reducing the cost of re-ranking the documents
retrieved by a traditional model, ColBERT’s pruning-friendly interaction mechanism enables leveraging vector-similarity indexes
for end-to-end retrieval directly from a large document collection.

We extensively evaluate ColBERT using two recent passage search
datasets.

To reconcile efficiency and contextualization in IR, we propose
ColBERT , a ranking model based on co ntextualized l ate interaction over BERT .

As the name suggests, ColBERT proposes a novel
late interaction paradigm for estimating relevance between a query
q and a document d .

Under late interaction, q and d are separately
encoded into two sets of contextual embeddings, and relevance is
evaluated using cheap and pruning-friendly computations between
both sets—that is, fast computations that enable ranking without
exhaustively evaluating every possible candidate.

Figure 2 contrasts our proposed late interaction approach with
existing neural matching paradigms.

On the left, Figure 2 (a) illustrates representation-focused rankers, which independently compute
an embedding for q and another for d and estimate relevance as
a single similarity score between two vectors [12, 41].

Moving to
the right, Figure 2 (b) visualizes typical interaction-focused rankers.

Instead of summarizing q and d into individual embeddings, these
rankers model word- and phrase-level relationships across q and d
and match them using a deep neural network (e.g., with CNNs/MLPs
[22] or kernels [36]).

In the simplest case, they feed the neural network an interaction matrix that reflects the similiarity between
every pair of words across q and d .

Language Model Pretraining for IR.

Recent work in NLU
emphasizes the importance pre-training language representation
models in an unsupervised fashion before subsequently fine-tuning
them on downstream tasks. A notable example is BERT [5], a bidirectional transformer-based language model whose fine-tuning
advanced the state of the art on various NLU benchmarks.

Nogueira et
al. [25], MacAvaney et al. [18], and Dai & Callan [3] investigate
incorporating such LMs (mainly BERT, but also ELMo [29]) on different ranking datasets.

As illustrated in Figure 2 (c), the common
approach (and the one adopted by Nogueira et al. on MS MARCO
and TREC CAR) is to feed the query–document pair through BERT
and use an MLP on top of BERT’s [CLS] output token to produce a
relevance score.

Subsequent work by Nogueira et al. [27] introduced
duoBERT, which fine-tunes BERT to compare the relevance of a
pair of documents given a query.

Relative to their single-document
BERT, this gives duoBERT a 1% MRR@10 advantage on MS MARCO
while increasing the cost by at least 1.4 × .

Concurrently with our drafting of this paper, Hofst¨ aer et al. [11]
published their Transformer-Kernel (TK) model.

At a high level, TK
improves the KNRM architecture described earlier: while KNRM
employs kernel pooling on top of word-embedding-based interaction, TK uses a Transformer [34] component for contextually

TK establishes a new state-of-the-art for non-BERT models on MS MARCO
(Dev); however, the best non-ensemble MRR@10 it achieves is 31%
while ColBERT reaches up to 36%.

Moreover, due to indexing document representations offline and employing a MaxSim-based late
interaction mechanism, ColBERT is much more scalable, enabling
end-to-end retrieval which is not supported by TK.
3 COLBERT
ColBERT prescribes a simple framework for balancing the quality
and cost of neural IR, particularly deep language models like BERT.

As introduced earlier, delaying the query–document interaction can
facilitate cheap neural re-ranking (i.e., through pre-computation)
and even support practical end-to-end neural retrieval (i.e., through
pruning via vector-similarity search).

ColBERT addresses how to
do so while still preserving the effectiveness of state-of-the-art
models, which condition the bulk of their computations on the
joint query–document pair.

Even though ColBERT’s late-interaction framework can be applied to a wide variety of architectures (e.g., CNNs, RNNs, transformers, etc.), we choose to focus this work on bi-directional transformerbased encoders (i.e., BERT) owing to their state-of-the-art effectiveness yet very high computational cost.
3.1 Architecture
Figure 3 depicts the general architecture of ColBERT, which comprises: (a) a query encoder f Q , (b) a document encoder f D , and (c)
the late interaction mechanism.

Given a query q and document d ,
f Q encodes q into a bag of fixed-size embeddings E q while f D encodes d into another bag E d .

Crucially, each embeddings in E q and
E d is contextualized based on the other terms in q or d , respectively.

We describe our BERT-based encoders in §3.2.

Using E q and E d , ColBERT computes the relevance score between q and d via late interaction, which we define as a summation
of maximum similarity (MaxSim) operators.

In particular, we find
the maximum cosine similarity of each v ∈ E q with vectors in E d ,
and combine the outputs via summation.

Besides cosine, we also
evaluate squared L2 distance as a measure of vector similarity.

Intuitively, this interaction mechanism softly searches for each query
term t q —in a manner that reflects its context in the query—against
the document’s embeddings, quantifying the strength of the “match”
via the largest similarity score between t q and a document term t d .

Given these term scores, it then estimates the document relevance
by summing the matching evidence across all query terms.

While more sophisticated matching is possible with other choices
such as deep convolution and aention layers (i.e., as in typical
interaction-focused models), a summation of maximum similarity
computations has two distinctive characteristics.

First, it stands
out as a particularly cheap interaction mechanism, as we examine
its FLOPs in §4.2.

Second, and more importantly, it is amenable
to highly-efficient pruning for top- k retrieval, as we evaluate in
§4.3.

This enables using vector-similarity algorithms for skipping
documents without materializing the full interaction matrix or even
considering each document in isolation.

Other cheap choices (e.g.,
a summation of average similarity scores, instead of maximum) are
possible; however, many are less amenable to pruning.

In §4.4, we
conduct an extensive ablation study that empirically verifies the advantage of our MaxSim-based late interaction against alternatives.

and documents by prepending a special token [Q] to queries and
another token [D] to documents.

3.4 Offline Indexing: Computing & Storing
Document Embeddings
By design, ColBERT isolates almost all of the computations between
queries and documents, largely to enable pre-computing document
representations offline.

At a high level, our indexing procedure is
straight-forward: we proceed over the documents in the collection
in batches, running our document encoder f D on each batch and
storing the output embeddings per document.

Although indexing
a set of documents is an offline process, we incorporate a few
simple optimizations for enhancing the throughput of indexing.

As
we show in §4.5, these optimizations can considerably reduce the
offline cost of indexing.

To begin with, we exploit multiple GPUs, if available, for faster
encoding of batches of documents in parallel.

encoding of batches of documents in parallel.

When batching, we
pad all documents to the maximum length of a document within
the batch. 3 To make capping the sequence length on a per-batch
basis more effective, our indexer proceeds through documents in
groups of B (e.g., B = 100,000) documents.

It sorts these documents
by length and then feeds batches of b (e.g., b = 128) documents of
comparable length through our encoder.

This length-based bucketing is sometimes refered to as a BucketIterator in some libraries
(e.g., allenNLP).

Lastly, while most computations occur on the GPU,
we found that a non-trivial portion of the indexing time is spent on
pre-processing the text sequences, primarily BERT’s WordPiece tokenization.

Exploiting that these operations are independent across
documents in a batch, we parallelize the pre-processing across the
available CPU cores.

Once the document representations are produced, they are saved
to disk using 32-bit or 16-bit values to represent each dimension.

As we describe in §3.5 and 3.6, these representations are either
simply loaded from disk for ranking or are subsequently indexed
for vector-similarity search, respectively.
3.5 Top- k Re-ranking with ColBERT
Recall that ColBERT can be used for re-ranking the output of another retrieval model, typically a term-based model, or directly
for end-to-end retrieval from a document collection.

Finally, we sort the k documents by their total scores.

Relative to existing neural rankers (especially, but not exclusively, BERT-based ones), this computation is very cheap that, in
fact, its cost is dominated by the cost of gathering and transferring

To illustrate, ranking k documents
via typical BERT rankers requires feeding BERT k different inputs

aention has quadratic cost in the length of the sequence.

In contrast, ColBERT feeds BERT only a single, much shorter sequence of

Consequently, ColBERT is not only cheaper, it also
scales much beer with k as we examine in §4.2.
3.6 End-to-end Top- k Retrieval with ColBERT
As mentioned before, ColBERT’s late-interaction operator is specifically designed to enable end-to-end retrieval from a large collection,
largely to improve recall relative to term-based retrieval approaches.

This section is concerned with cases where the number of documents to be ranked is too large for exhaustive evaluation of each
possible candidate document, particularly when we are only interested in the highest scoring ones.

Concretely, we focus here on
retrieving the top- k results directly from a large document collection with N (e.g., N = 10 , 000 , 000) documents, where k  N .

To do so, we leverage the pruning-friendly nature of the MaxSim
operations at the backbone of late interaction.

Moreover,
the index conducts the similarity computations in this compressed

ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via
Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
Omar Khaab
Stanford University
okhaab@stanford.edu
Matei Zaharia
Stanford University
matei@cs.stanford.edu
ABSTRACT
Recent progress in Natural Language Understanding (NLU) is driving fast-paced advances in Information Retrieval (IR), largely owed
to fine-tuning deep language models (LMs) for document ranking.

While remarkably effective, the ranking models based on these LMs
increase computational cost by orders of magnitude over prior approaches, particularly as they must feed each query–document pair
through a massive neural network to compute a single relevance
score.

To tackle this, we present ColBERT, a novel ranking model
that adapts deep LMs (in particular, BERT) for efficient retrieval.

ColBERT introduces a late interaction architecture that independently encodes the query and the document using BERT and then
employs a cheap yet powerful interaction step that models their
fine-grained similarity.

By delaying and yet retaining this finegranular interaction, ColBERT can leverage the expressiveness of
deep LMs while simultaneously gaining the ability to pre-compute
document representations offline, considerably speeding up query
processing.

Beyond reducing the cost of re-ranking the documents
retrieved by a traditional model, ColBERT’s pruning-friendly interaction mechanism enables leveraging vector-similarity indexes
for end-to-end retrieval directly from a large document collection.

We extensively evaluate ColBERT using two recent passage search
datasets.

To reconcile efficiency and contextualization in IR, we propose
ColBERT , a ranking model based on co ntextualized l ate interaction over BERT .

As the name suggests, ColBERT proposes a novel
late interaction paradigm for estimating relevance between a query
q and a document d .

Under late interaction, q and d are separately
encoded into two sets of contextual embeddings, and relevance is
evaluated using cheap and pruning-friendly computations between
both sets—that is, fast computations that enable ranking without
exhaustively evaluating every possible candidate.

Figure 2 contrasts our proposed late interaction approach with
existing neural matching paradigms.

On the left, Figure 2 (a) illustrates representation-focused rankers, which independently compute
an embedding for q and another for d and estimate relevance as
a single similarity score between two vectors [12, 41].

Moving to
the right, Figure 2 (b) visualizes typical interaction-focused rankers.

Instead of summarizing q and d into individual embeddings, these
rankers model word- and phrase-level relationships across q and d
and match them using a deep neural network (e.g., with CNNs/MLPs
[22] or kernels [36]).

In the simplest case, they feed the neural network an interaction matrix that reflects the similiarity between
every pair of words across q and d .

3 COLBERT
ColBERT prescribes a simple framework for balancing the quality
and cost of neural IR, particularly deep language models like BERT.

As introduced earlier, delaying the query–document interaction can
facilitate cheap neural re-ranking (i.e., through pre-computation)
and even support practical end-to-end neural retrieval (i.e., through
pruning via vector-similarity search).

ColBERT addresses how to
do so while still preserving the effectiveness of state-of-the-art
models, which condition the bulk of their computations on the
joint query–document pair.

Even though ColBERT’s late-interaction framework can be applied to a wide variety of architectures (e.g., CNNs, RNNs, transformers, etc.), we choose to focus this work on bi-directional transformerbased encoders (i.e., BERT) owing to their state-of-the-art effectiveness yet very high computational cost.
3.1 Architecture
Figure 3 depicts the general architecture of ColBERT, which comprises: (a) a query encoder f Q , (b) a document encoder f D , and (c)
the late interaction mechanism.

Given a query q and document d ,
f Q encodes q into a bag of fixed-size embeddings E q while f D encodes d into another bag E d .

Crucially, each embeddings in E q and
E d is contextualized based on the other terms in q or d , respectively.

We describe our BERT-based encoders in §3.2.

Using E q and E d , ColBERT computes the relevance score between q and d via late interaction, which we define as a summation
of maximum similarity (MaxSim) operators.

In particular, we find
the maximum cosine similarity of each v ∈ E q with vectors in E d ,
and combine the outputs via summation.

Besides cosine, we also
evaluate squared L2 distance as a measure of vector similarity.

Intuitively, this interaction mechanism softly searches for each query
term t q —in a manner that reflects its context in the query—against
the document’s embeddings, quantifying the strength of the “match”
via the largest similarity score between t q and a document term t d .

Given these term scores, it then estimates the document relevance
by summing the matching evidence across all query terms.

Document Embeddings
By design, ColBERT isolates almost all of the computations between
queries and documents, largely to enable pre-computing document
representations offline.

At a high level, our indexing procedure is
straight-forward: we proceed over the documents in the collection
in batches, running our document encoder f D on each batch and
storing the output embeddings per document.

Although indexing
a set of documents is an offline process, we incorporate a few
simple optimizations for enhancing the throughput of indexing.

As
we show in §4.5, these optimizations can considerably reduce the
offline cost of indexing.

To begin with, we exploit multiple GPUs, if available, for faster
encoding of batches of documents in parallel.

To begin with, we exploit multiple GPUs, if available, for faster

When batching, we

It sorts these documents

This length-based bucketing is sometimes refered to as a BucketIterator in some libraries
(e.g., allenNLP).

Lastly, while most computations occur on the GPU,
we found that a non-trivial portion of the indexing time is spent on
pre-processing the text sequences, primarily BERT’s WordPiece tokenization.

Exploiting that these operations are independent across
documents in a batch, we parallelize the pre-processing across the
available CPU cores.

Once the document representations are produced, they are saved
to disk using 32-bit or 16-bit values to represent each dimension.

As we describe in §3.5 and 3.6, these representations are either
simply loaded from disk for ranking or are subsequently indexed
for vector-similarity search, respectively.

This section is concerned with cases where the number of documents to be ranked is too large for exhaustive evaluation of each
possible candidate document, particularly when we are only interested in the highest scoring ones.

ABSTRACT
Recent progress in Natural Language Understanding (NLU) is driving fast-paced advances in Information Retrieval (IR), largely owed
to fine-tuning deep language models (LMs) for document ranking.

While remarkably effective, the ranking models based on these LMs
increase computational cost by orders of magnitude over prior approaches, particularly as they must feed each query–document pair
through a massive neural network to compute a single relevance
score.

To tackle this, we present ColBERT, a novel ranking model
that adapts deep LMs (in particular, BERT) for efficient retrieval.

ColBERT introduces a late interaction architecture that independently encodes the query and the document using BERT and then
employs a cheap yet powerful interaction step that models their
fine-grained similarity.

By delaying and yet retaining this finegranular interaction, ColBERT can leverage the expressiveness of
deep LMs while simultaneously gaining the ability to pre-compute
document representations offline, considerably speeding up query
processing.

Beyond reducing the cost of re-ranking the documents
retrieved by a traditional model, ColBERT’s pruning-friendly interaction mechanism enables leveraging vector-similarity indexes
for end-to-end retrieval directly from a large document collection.

We extensively evaluate ColBERT using two recent passage search
datasets.

To reconcile efficiency and contextualization in IR, we propose
ColBERT , a ranking model based on co ntextualized l ate interaction over BERT .

As the name suggests, ColBERT proposes a novel
late interaction paradigm for estimating relevance between a query
q and a document d .

Under late interaction, q and d are separately
encoded into two sets of contextual embeddings, and relevance is
evaluated using cheap and pruning-friendly computations between
both sets—that is, fast computations that enable ranking without
exhaustively evaluating every possible candidate.

Figure 2 contrasts our proposed late interaction approach with
existing neural matching paradigms.

On the left, Figure 2 (a) illustrates representation-focused rankers, which independently compute
an embedding for q and another for d and estimate relevance as
a single similarity score between two vectors [12, 41].

Moving to
the right, Figure 2 (b) visualizes typical interaction-focused rankers.

Instead of summarizing q and d into individual embeddings, these
rankers model word- and phrase-level relationships across q and d
and match them using a deep neural network (e.g., with CNNs/MLPs
[22] or kernels [36]).

In the simplest case, they feed the neural network an interaction matrix that reflects the similiarity between
every pair of words across q and d .

Language Model Pretraining for IR.

Recent work in NLU
emphasizes the importance pre-training language representation
models in an unsupervised fashion before subsequently fine-tuning
them on downstream tasks. A notable example is BERT [5], a bidirectional transformer-based language model whose fine-tuning
advanced the state of the art on various NLU benchmarks.

Nogueira et
al. [25], MacAvaney et al. [18], and Dai & Callan [3] investigate
incorporating such LMs (mainly BERT, but also ELMo [29]) on different ranking datasets.

As illustrated in Figure 2 (c), the common
approach (and the one adopted by Nogueira et al. on MS MARCO
and TREC CAR) is to feed the query–document pair through BERT
and use an MLP on top of BERT’s [CLS] output token to produce a
relevance score.

Subsequent work by Nogueira et al. [27] introduced

Relative to their single-document

At a high level, TK

Moreover, due to indexing document representations offline and employing a MaxSim-based late

3 COLBERT
ColBERT prescribes a simple framework for balancing the quality
and cost of neural IR, particularly deep language models like BERT.

As introduced earlier, delaying the query–document interaction can
facilitate cheap neural re-ranking (i.e., through pre-computation)
and even support practical end-to-end neural retrieval (i.e., through
pruning via vector-similarity search).

ColBERT addresses how to
do so while still preserving the effectiveness of state-of-the-art
models, which condition the bulk of their computations on the
joint query–document pair.

原文：Even though ColBERT’s late-interaction framework can be applied to a wide variety of architectures (e.g., CNNs, RNNs, transformers, etc.), we choose to focus this work on bi-directional transformerbased encoders (i.e., BERT) owing to their state-of-the-art effectiveness yet very high computational cost.
3.1 Architecture
Figure 3 depicts the general architecture of ColBERT, which comprises: (a) a query encoder f Q , (b) a document encoder f D , and (c)
the late interaction mechanism.

Given a query q and document d ,
f Q encodes q into a bag of fixed-size embeddings E q while f D encodes d into another bag E d .

Crucially, each embeddings in E q and
E d is contextualized based on the other terms in q or d , respectively.

We describe our BERT-based encoders in §3.2.

Using E q and E d , ColBERT computes the relevance score between q and d via late interaction, which we define as a summation
of maximum similarity (MaxSim) operators.

In particular, we find
the maximum cosine similarity of each v ∈ E q with vectors in E d ,
and combine the outputs via summation.

Besides cosine, we also
evaluate squared L2 distance as a measure of vector similarity.

Intuitively, this interaction mechanism softly searches for each query
term t q —in a manner that reflects its context in the query—against
the document’s embeddings, quantifying the strength of the “match”
via the largest similarity score between t q and a document term t d .

Given these term scores, it then estimates the document relevance
by summing the matching evidence across all query terms.

Given these term scores, it then estimates the document relevance

While more sophisticated matching is possible with other choices
such as deep convolution and aention layers (i.e., as in typical
interaction-focused models), a summation of maximum similarity
computations has two distinctive characteristics.

First, it stands
out as a particularly cheap interaction mechanism, as we examine
its FLOPs in §4.2.

Second, and more importantly, it is amenable
to highly-efficient pruning for top- k retrieval, as we evaluate in
§4.3.

This enables using vector-similarity algorithms for skipping
documents without materializing the full interaction matrix or even
considering each document in isolation.

Other cheap choices (e.g.,
a summation of average similarity scores, instead of maximum) are
possible; however, many are less amenable to pruning.

In §4.4, we
conduct an extensive ablation study that empirically verifies the advantage of our MaxSim-based late interaction against alternatives.

Prior to late interaction, ColBERT encodes each query or document
into a bag of embeddings, employing BERT-based encoders.

We
share a single BERT model among our query and document encoders but distinguish input sequences that correspond to queries
and documents by prepending a special token [Q] to queries and
another token [D] to documents.

3.4 Offline Indexing: Computing & Storing
Document Embeddings
By design, ColBERT isolates almost all of the computations between
queries and documents, largely to enable pre-computing document
representations offline.

At a high level, our indexing procedure is
straight-forward: we proceed over the documents in the collection
in batches, running our document encoder f D on each batch and
storing the output embeddings per document.

Although indexing
a set of documents is an offline process, we incorporate a few
simple optimizations for enhancing the throughput of indexing.

As
we show in §4.5, these optimizations can considerably reduce the
offline cost of indexing.

To begin with, we exploit multiple GPUs, if available, for faster
encoding of batches of documents in parallel.

This length-based bucketing is sometimes refered to as a BucketIterator in some libraries

Lastly, while most computations occur on the GPU,

Exploiting that these operations are independent across

Once the document representations are produced, they are saved
to disk using 32-bit or 16-bit values to represent each dimension.

As we describe in §3.5 and 3.6, these representations are either
simply loaded from disk for ranking or are subsequently indexed
for vector-similarity search, respectively.

3.6 End-to-end Top- k Retrieval with ColBERT
As mentioned before, ColBERT’s late-interaction operator is specifically designed to enable end-to-end retrieval from a large collection,
largely to improve recall relative to term-based retrieval approaches.

This section is concerned with cases where the number of documents to be ranked is too large for exhaustive evaluation of each
possible candidate document, particularly when we are only interested in the highest scoring ones.

Concretely, we focus here on
retrieving the top- k results directly from a large document collection with N (e.g., N = 10 , 000 , 000) documents, where k  N .

To do so, we leverage the pruning-friendly nature of the MaxSim
operations at the backbone of late interaction.

In our faiss -based implementation, we use an IVFPQ index (“inverted file with product quantization”).

This index partitions the

Moreover,
the index conducts the similarity computations in this compressed
domain, leading to cheaper computations and thus faster search.

- ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
  - 研究动机
    - 基于深度语言模型（如BERT）的排序模型虽然有效，但计算成本高昂，比先前方法高100-1000倍。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3] [evidence-5-f4a4a306-902d-41ed-bcdc-bcc8270b5f83]
    - 这种“质量-成本权衡”带来了严峻挑战，因为查询响应时间增加100ms就会影响用户体验并减少收入。 [evidence-7-f724b401-34db-482a-8b40-237d2476f1ca]
    - 现有尝试使用NLU技术增强传统模型（如BM25）的方法，虽然降低了延迟，但精度相对于BERT有显著降低。 [evidence-7-f724b401-34db-482a-8b40-237d2476f1ca]
    - 因此，需要一种能够协调效率与上下文化的排序模型。 [evidence-8-682b5a48-0813-4b5b-8f4a-5847bb59c9e2]
  - 问题定义
    - 设计一个既高效又有效的段落检索排序模型。
      - 降低基于BERT的模型的计算成本。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3]
      - 保持与现有BERT模型竞争性的效果。 [evidence-3-cb82273a-7e49-4c21-941e-d3f0d2759209]
      - 支持重排序和端到端检索两种模式。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3]
  - 关键假设
    - 后期交互：将查询和文档的交互延迟到分别编码之后，通过一个廉价计算步骤来评估相关性，可以同时保留深度LM的表现力和实现高效的预计算。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3] [evidence-10-3b06f8a2-71c9-48df-a218-c7cf9035ffe5]
    - MaxSim：对每个查询嵌入，在文档嵌入集合中取最大相似度后求和，是一个既廉价又有利于剪枝的交互机制。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
    - 过滤标点：文档编码后移除标点符号对应的嵌入，可以降低存储开销而不影响效果。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
    - 离线预计算：文档表示可以离线预计算并存储，以加快查询处理速度。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3]
    - IVFPQ参数：通过k-means划分、子向量量化和近邻搜索，可以在大规模文档集合中实现高效的近似检索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
    - 单查询编码：ColBERT仅对查询进行一次BERT编码，而传统模型需要对每个查询-文档对编码。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7]
  - 数据流
    - 查询编码
      - 输入：查询词序列q0, q1, ..., ql。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 处理：添加特殊标记[Q]和[CLS]，并通过[mask]标记补足到固定长度。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 编码：通过共享的BERT模型和线性层生成上下文嵌入。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
      - 输出：经过L2归一化的固定大小的嵌入袋Eq。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be] [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
    - 文档编码（离线）
      - 输入：文档词序列d0, d1, ..., dn。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 处理：添加特殊标记[D]和[CLS]，不加[mask]。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be]
      - 编码：通过共享的BERT模型和线性层生成上下文嵌入。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
      - 过滤：移除标点符号对应的嵌入。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 输出：经过L2归一化的嵌入袋Ed。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be]
    - 评分（后期交互）
      - 输入：Eq和Ed。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 计算：对Eq中的每个嵌入，计算其与Ed中所有嵌入的点积（因L2归一化，等价于余弦相似度），取最大值，然后将所有最大值求和。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 输出：相关性得分Sq,d。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
    - 索引（离线）
      - 批量处理文档，使用多GPU、长度分桶、多核预处理等优化。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]
      - 以32-bit或16-bit浮点数将文档嵌入保存到磁盘。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]
      - 可选：构建IVFPQ索引以支持端到端检索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
    - 端到端检索 (两阶段)
      - 第一阶段 (近似检索)：使用IVFPQ索引，对每个查询嵌入搜索邻近单元，合并得到候选文档集K。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - 第二阶段 (精确重排序)：对候选集K使用标准ColBERT重排序步骤。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
  - 算法步骤
    - 训练
      - 使用三元组 (q, d+, d-) 进行训练。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 损失函数：成对softmax交叉熵损失。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 优化器：Adam。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 微调：共享的BERT模型、线性层和特殊标记[Q]、[D]的嵌入。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 注意：交互机制（MaxSim）本身无可训练参数。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
    - 重排序
      - 使用BM25等模型检索出top-k文档。 [evidence-6-6e1dee63-f411-44ce-b0fe-f4a78524083d]
      - 从磁盘/索引加载这些文档的预计算嵌入。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7]
      - 对查询进行实时编码。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7]
      - 执行穷举MaxSim计算。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7]
      - 按得分排序，输出最终的top-k文档。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7]
    - 端到端检索
      - 构建IVFPQ索引。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - 查询阶段1：近似搜索候选文档。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - 查询阶段2：精确重排序候选文档。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
  - 公式/变量
    - 公式(1): Eq = Normalize(CNN(BERT("[Q] q0 q1 ... ql ##... #"))) [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - q0, q1, ..., ql: 查询词序列。
      - ##... #: 用于补足查询到固定长度的[mask]标记。
      - CNN: 用于降维的线性层。
      - Normalize: L2归一化。
      - BERT: 共享的BERT编码器。
    - 公式(2): Ed = Filter(Normalize(CNN(BERT("[D] d0, d1, ..., dn")))) [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - d0, d1, ..., dn: 文档词序列。
      - Filter: 移除标点符号嵌入。
    - 公式(3): S_q,d = Σ_{i∈[|Eq|]} max_{j∈[|Ed|]} (Eq_i · Ed^T_j) [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - S_q,d: 查询q和文档d的相关性得分。
      - |Eq|: 查询嵌入的数量。
      - |Ed|: 文档嵌入的数量。
      - ·: 点积（因归一化，等价于余弦相似度）。
    - 关键变量
      - m: 线性层输出的嵌入维度，远小于BERT的隐藏维度，用于控制存储。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be]
      - l: 查询的token数量。
      - n: 文档的token数量。
      - max_q: 查询补足后的固定长度。
      - P: IVFPQ索引中聚类中心的数量（默认为2000）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - p: 每个查询嵌入搜索的邻近单元数（默认为10）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - k': 每个查询嵌入在近似检索中返回的嵌入数（默认为1000）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - k: 最终返回的文档数（默认为1000）。
      - s: 每个嵌入被分割的子向量数（默认为16）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - B: 索引时长度分桶的组大小（默认为100,000）。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]
      - b: 索引时每批处理的文档数（默认为128）。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]
      - N: 文档集合大小（示例中为10,000,000）。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7]
  - 模型与组件
    - ColBERT架构
      - 查询编码器 f_Q: 将查询编码为嵌入袋Eq。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
      - 文档编码器 f_D: 将文档编码为嵌入袋Ed。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
      - 后期交互机制: 使用MaxSim计算相关性得分。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
    - BERT (基础编码器)
      - 作用：为查询和文档生成上下文感知的嵌入。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 共享：查询和文档编码器共享同一个BERT模型。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
      - 区分：通过不同的特殊标记（[Q]和[D]）来区分输入序列类型。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
    - 线性层 (CNN)
      - 作用：将BERT的输出维度降低到更小的m维度，以控制存储和传输开销。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be]
    - MaxSim操作
      - 什么是MaxSim: 一个求和的最大相似度操作。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 在方法中的位置：它是后期交互的核心，在查询和文档独立编码后执行。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 与相邻概念的关系：
        - 它替代了传统模型中的全交互矩阵或注意力层。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
        - 它的求和特性比平均相似度更有利，因为强调了词条的最大匹配，且更有利于剪枝。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
    - 嵌入袋 (Bag of Embeddings)
      - 什么是嵌入袋：一个无序的嵌入向量集合，每个向量对应一个token的上下文表示。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 在方法中的位置：查询和文档编码器的输出，作为后期交互的输入。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
    - IVFPQ索引
      - 什么是IVFPQ: 一种基于倒排文件和乘积量化的向量索引，用于大规模近似最近邻搜索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - 在方法中的位置：用于实现ColBERT的端到端检索，在执行MaxSim前先快速筛选候选文档。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - 与相邻概念的关系：
        - 它利用了ColBERT的MaxSim操作适合剪枝的特性。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
        - 它将向量空间划分为多个单元以加速搜索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]

    - TREC CAR
      - 规模：包含约2900万段落和300万查询。 [evidence-19-fa2b4656-5462-4043-babd-ac3a880e20cf]

  - 指标
    - MRR@10 (Mean Reciprocal Rank at 10)
      - 定义：计算前10个检索结果中第一个相关文档的排名的倒数平均值。 [evidence-7-f724b401-34db-482a-8b40-237d2476f1ca]
      - 用途：用于评估排序效果，是MS MARCO的官方指标。 [evidence-19-fa2b4656-5462-4043-babd-ac3a880e20cf]
    - 查询延迟 (Query Latency)
      - 定义：处理一个查询所需的平均时间，以毫秒计。 [evidence-5-f4a4a306-902d-41ed-bcdc-bcc8270b5f83]
    - FLOPs (Floating Point Operations)
      - 定义：浮点运算次数，用于衡量计算量。 [evidence-3-cb82273a-7e49-4c21-941e-d3f0d2759209]
  - 定量结果
    - MS MARCO重排序结果
      - 模型[E] (ColBERT, 完整BERT): MRR@10 = 34.9%。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
      - 模型[D] (ColBERT, 5层BERT): MRR@10 未报告具体数值，但用于消融实验。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
      - 与BERT base对比：效果有竞争力或更优。 [evidence-3-cb82273a-7e49-4c21-941e-d3f0d2759209]
      - 与BERT large对比：延迟低90倍，FLOPs低13,900倍。 [evidence-22-684900fc-4d69-4780-b816-f7973b7aeeac]
      - 与现有BERT模型对比：速度快2个数量级，FLOPs少4个数量级。 [evidence-3-cb82273a-7e49-4c21-941e-d3f0d2759209]
      - 与docTTTTTquery对比：效果更好（ColBERT MRR@10=34.9%，docTTTTTquery为BM25+9%）。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
      - 与TK模型对比：ColBERT MRR@10高达36%，TK最高为31%。 [evidence-10-3b06f8a2-71c9-48df-a218-c7cf9035ffe5]
    - MS MARCO端到端检索结果 (ColBERT L2)
      - MRR@10: 低于重排序版本，但能检索到BM25 top-1000中完全遗漏的文档。 [evidence-25-f93fb999-b190-4bc7-b4f0-4145e057edd5]
      - 能够检索到被BM25 top-1000完全遗漏的top-10文档。 [evidence-25-f93fb999-b190-4bc7-b4f0-4145e057edd5]
    - 延迟对比 (Table 2)
      - BM25 (Anserini): MRR@10 = 18.7，延迟极低。 [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
      - docTTTTTquery: MRR@10比BM25高9%，延迟几乎无增加（基于BM25）。 [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
      - ColBERT重排序延迟略高于非BERT重排序模型，但查询编码和交互本身仅需13毫秒。 [evidence-22-684900fc-4d69-4780-b816-f7973b7aeeac]
      - ColBERT端到端检索延迟高于重排序，但支持全库索引。
    - 索引吞吐量 (Figure 6)
      - 通过优化（多GPU、长度分桶等），可在约3小时内索引完MS MARCO数据集。 [evidence-25-f93fb999-b190-4bc7-b4f0-4145e057edd5]
  - 消融 (Ablation)
    - 模型[A] (单向量内积): 效果远不如ColBERT，证明了后期交互细粒度匹配的必要性。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
      - 该模型将查询和文档分别编码为一个4096维的向量（来自[CLS]标记），然后计算内积。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
    - 模型[B] (平均相似度): 效果低于最大相似度，说明查询词需要特别关注文档中的特定词。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
    - 模型[C] (无查询扩展): MRR@10显著降低，证明了查询扩展（增加[mask]标记）的重要性。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
    - 模型[D] (5层BERT vs. 12层BERT): 由于训练成本，消融模型基于5层BERT训练，但其效果低于完整12层模型[E]。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
      - Tokenization: BERT的WordPiece分词在索引过程中占据显著开销，限制了进一步提速。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]
    - 降维和量化：通过减小向量维度(m)和量化（从32-bit到16-bit），可以显著降低延迟和存储，但会影响一定的MRR@10。 [evidence-22-684900fc-4d69-4780-b816-f7973b7aeeac]
  - 效率
    - 单线程延迟：ColBERT的重排序延迟在单线程下测量。 [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
    - 查询延迟瓶颈：主要开销在于从CPU内存收集和传输预计算的文档嵌入到GPU，而非查询编码和交互本身（仅13ms）。 [evidence-22-684900fc-4d69-4780-b816-f7973b7aeeac]
    - FLOPs：ColBERT的FLOPs比BERT large低13,900倍，比非BERT模型稍高，但主要是传输开销。 [evidence-22-684900fc-4d69-4780-b816-f7973b7aeeac]
    - 索引吞吐量：通过在索引阶段使用多GPU、长度分桶、多核预处理等优化，可以在约3小时内索引完MS MARCO。 [evidence-25-f93fb999-b190-4bc7-b4f0-4145e057edd5]
    - 并行化：可以通过将索引分片并在多个机器上并行化来进一步降低已经较低的延迟。 [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
  - 失败模式
    - gather瓶颈：重排序时，收集和传输文档嵌入到GPU的开销占主导地位，甚至可能超过计算本身。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7] [evidence-22-684900fc-4d69-4780-b816-f7973b7aeeac]
    - faiss参数敏感性：IVFPQ索引的性能和召回率高度依赖于参数选择（P, p, s），不合适的参数可能导致精度损失。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
    - 度量不一致性：重排序使用余弦相似度，端到端检索使用L2距离，可能导致度量不一致。 [evidence-20-a3a21a22-a918-4448-b8d3-5d714b5954e8]
    - 训练成本：训练完整12层BERT模型的计算成本高昂，导致消融实验只能基于5层BERT。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
  - 局限
    - 存储与吞吐量
      - 文档索引需要大量存储空间，但通过降维（m远小于BERT隐藏维度）和量化可以有效控制。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be]
      - 索引吞吐量受限于CPU预处理（WordPiece分词）。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]
    - 检索时延
      - 虽然比BERT模型快很多，但重排序延迟仍比非BERT模型高几十毫秒。 [evidence-22-684900fc-4d69-4780-b816-f7973b7aeeac]
      - 端到端检索虽然能覆盖BM25的遗漏，但MRR@10低于重排序版本。
    - 近似精度损失
      - IVFPQ在低资源（如使用16-bit）或高压缩率下，可能会丢失一些高相似度的文档，导致召回损失。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
    - 实验设定约束
      - 部分实验使用5层BERT，无法完全代表12层模型的性能。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
      - 延迟测量仅在单线程环境下进行，未考虑多线程并行化的优势。 [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
    - 理论分析缺失
      - 论文没有提供MaxSim操作的理论保证，主要依赖实验验证。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 过滤标点符号的有效性仅通过消融验证，缺乏理论解释。
  - 可复现信息

answer:
- ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
  - 研究动机
    - 基于深度语言模型（如BERT）的排序模型虽然有效，但计算成本高昂，比先前方法高100-1000倍。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3] [evidence-5-f4a4a306-902d-41ed-bcdc-bcc8270b5f83]
    - 这种“质量-成本权衡”带来了严峻挑战，因为查询响应时间增加100ms就会影响用户体验并减少收入。 [evidence-7-f724b401-34db-482a-8b40-237d2476f1ca]
    - 现有尝试使用NLU技术增强传统模型（如BM25）的方法，虽然降低了延迟，但精度相对于BERT有显著降低。 [evidence-7-f724b401-34db-482a-8b40-237d2476f1ca]
    - 因此，需要一种能够协调效率与上下文化的排序模型。 [evidence-8-682b5a48-0813-4b5b-8f4a-5847bb59c9e2]
  - 问题定义
    - 设计一个既高效又有效的段落检索排序模型。
      - 降低基于BERT的模型的计算成本。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3]
      - 保持与现有BERT模型竞争性的效果。 [evidence-3-cb82273a-7e49-4c21-941e-d3f0d2759209]
      - 支持重排序和端到端检索两种模式。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3]
  - 关键假设
    - 后期交互：将查询和文档的交互延迟到分别编码之后，通过一个廉价计算步骤来评估相关性，可以同时保留深度LM的表现力和实现高效的预计算。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3] [evidence-10-3b06f8a2-71c9-48df-a218-c7cf9035ffe5]
    - MaxSim：对每个查询嵌入，在文档嵌入集合中取最大相似度后求和，是一个既廉价又有利于剪枝的交互机制。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
    - 过滤标点：文档编码后移除标点符号对应的嵌入，可以降低存储开销而不影响效果。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
    - 离线预计算：文档表示可以离线预计算并存储，以加快查询处理速度。 [evidence-2-fbc190bc-7be2-43a3-8eae-a352c9fecee3]
    - IVFPQ参数：通过k-means划分、子向量量化和近邻搜索，可以在大规模文档集合中实现高效的近似检索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
    - 单查询编码：ColBERT仅对查询进行一次BERT编码，而传统模型需要对每个查询-文档对编码。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7]
  - 数据流
    - 查询编码
      - 输入：查询词序列q0, q1, ..., ql。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 处理：添加特殊标记[Q]和[CLS]，并通过[mask]标记补足到固定长度。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 编码：通过共享的BERT模型和线性层生成上下文嵌入。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
      - 输出：经过L2归一化的固定大小的嵌入袋Eq。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be] [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
    - 文档编码（离线）
      - 输入：文档词序列d0, d1, ..., dn。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 处理：添加特殊标记[D]和[CLS]，不加[mask]。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be]
      - 编码：通过共享的BERT模型和线性层生成上下文嵌入。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
      - 过滤：移除标点符号对应的嵌入。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - 输出：经过L2归一化的嵌入袋Ed。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be]
    - 评分（后期交互）
      - 输入：Eq和Ed。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 计算：对Eq中的每个嵌入，计算其与Ed中所有嵌入的点积（因L2归一化，等价于余弦相似度），取最大值，然后将所有最大值求和。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 输出：相关性得分Sq,d。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
    - 索引（离线）
      - 批量处理文档，使用多GPU、长度分桶、多核预处理等优化。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]
      - 以32-bit或16-bit浮点数将文档嵌入保存到磁盘。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]
      - 可选：构建IVFPQ索引以支持端到端检索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]

      - 第二阶段 (精确重排序)：对候选集K使用标准ColBERT重排序步骤。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
  - 算法步骤
    - 训练
      - 使用三元组 (q, d+, d-) 进行训练。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 损失函数：成对softmax交叉熵损失。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 优化器：Adam。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - 微调：共享的BERT模型、线性层和特殊标记[Q]、[D]的嵌入。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]

      - 从磁盘/索引加载这些文档的预计算嵌入。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7]

      - 查询阶段2：精确重排序候选文档。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
  - 公式/变量
    - 公式(1): Eq = Normalize(CNN(BERT("[Q] q0 q1 ... ql ##... #"))) [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - q0, q1, ..., ql: 查询词序列。
      - ##... #: 用于补足查询到固定长度的[mask]标记。
      - CNN: 用于降维的线性层。
      - Normalize: L2归一化。
      - BERT: 共享的BERT编码器。
    - 公式(2): Ed = Filter(Normalize(CNN(BERT("[D] d0, d1, ..., dn")))) [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8]
      - d0, d1, ..., dn: 文档词序列。
      - Filter: 移除标点符号嵌入。
    - 公式(3): S_q,d = Σ_{i∈[|Eq|]} max_{j∈[|Ed|]} (Eq_i · Ed^T_j) [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089]
      - S_q,d: 查询q和文档d的相关性得分。
      - |Eq|: 查询嵌入的数量。
      - |Ed|: 文档嵌入的数量。
      - ·: 点积（因归一化，等价于余弦相似度）。
    - 关键变量

      - l: 查询的token数量。
      - n: 文档的token数量。
      - max_q: 查询补足后的固定长度。
      - P: IVFPQ索引中聚类中心的数量（默认为2000）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - p: 每个查询嵌入搜索的邻近单元数（默认为10）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - k': 每个查询嵌入在近似检索中返回的嵌入数（默认为1000）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - k: 最终返回的文档数（默认为1000）。
      - s: 每个嵌入被分割的子向量数（默认为16）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - B: 索引时长度分桶的组大小（默认为100,000）。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12]

      - 文档编码器 f_D: 将文档编码为嵌入袋Ed。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]

    - BERT (基础编码器)
      - 作用：为查询和文档生成上下文感知的嵌入。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 共享：查询和文档编码器共享同一个BERT模型。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
      - 区分：通过不同的特殊标记（[Q]和[D]）来区分输入序列类型。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
    - 线性层 (CNN)
      - 作用：将BERT的输出维度降低到更小的m维度，以控制存储和传输开销。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be]
    - MaxSim操作
      - 什么是MaxSim: 一个求和的最大相似度操作。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 在方法中的位置：它是后期交互的核心，在查询和文档独立编码后执行。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 与相邻概念的关系：
        - 它替代了传统模型中的全交互矩阵或注意力层。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
        - 它的求和特性比平均相似度更有利，因为强调了词条的最大匹配，且更有利于剪枝。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
    - 嵌入袋 (Bag of Embeddings)
      - 什么是嵌入袋：一个无序的嵌入向量集合，每个向量对应一个token的上下文表示。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
      - 在方法中的位置：查询和文档编码器的输出，作为后期交互的输入。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f]
    - IVFPQ索引
      - 什么是IVFPQ: 一种基于倒排文件和乘积量化的向量索引，用于大规模近似最近邻搜索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - 在方法中的位置：用于实现ColBERT的端到端检索，在执行MaxSim前先快速筛选候选文档。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
      - 与相邻概念的关系：
        - 它利用了ColBERT的MaxSim操作适合剪枝的特性。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb]
        - 它将向量空间划分为多个单元以加速搜索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084]
  - 数据集
    - MS MARCO Passage Ranking
      - 规模：包含900万段落和100万查询。 [evidence-5-f4a4a306-902d-41ed-bcdc-bcc8270b5f83]

    - TREC CAR
      - 规模：包含约2900万段落和300万查询。 [evidence-19-fa2b4656-5462-4043-babd-ac3a880e20cf]
      - 来源：基于Wikipedia的合成数据集。 [evidence-19-fa2b4656-5462-4043-babd-ac3a880e20cf]

      - 数据划分：使用前4折（fold）进行训练，第5折进行验证。 [evidence-19-fa2b4656-5462-4043-babd-ac3a880e20cf]
  - 基线 (Baselines)
    - BM25 (Anserini实现) [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
    - doc2query [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
    - DeepCT [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
    - docTTTTTquery (基于T5) [evidence-23-5f9d8819-576a-4604-8563-841131a219b1]
    - KNRM [evidence-21-15dbc68c-bc37-44d3-969c-220528ec29bf]
    - Duet (及其更新版本) [evidence-21-15dbc68c-bc37-44d3-969c-220528ec29bf]
    - fastText + ConvKNRM [evidence-21-15dbc68c-bc37-44d3-969c-220528ec29bf]
    - Transformer-Kernel (TK) [evidence-10-3b06f8a2-71c9-48df-a218-c7cf9035ffe5]
    - BERT base [evidence-21-15dbc68c-bc37-44d3-969c-220528ec29bf]
    - BERT large [evidence-21-15dbc68c-bc37-44d3-969c-220528ec29bf]
    - duoBERT [evidence-9-e0c620c1-60c2-4b7c-8ddf-4109fa5d9258]
  - 指标
    - MRR@10 (Mean Reciprocal Rank at 10)
      - 定义：计算前10个检索结果中第一个相关文档的排名的倒数平均值。 [evidence-7-f724b401-34db-482a-8b40-237d2476f1ca]
      - 用途：用于评估排序效果，是MS MARCO的官方指标。 [evidence-19-fa2b4656-5462-4043-babd-ac3a880e20cf]
    - 查询延迟 (Query Latency)
      - 定义：处理一个查询所需的平均时间，以毫秒计。 [evidence-5-f4a4a306-902d-41ed-bcdc-bcc8270b5f83]
    - FLOPs (Floating Point Operations)
      - 定义：浮点运算次数，用于衡量计算量。 [evidence-3-cb82273a-7e49-4c21-941e-d3f0d2759209]
  - 定量结果
    - MS MARCO重排序结果
      - 模型[E] (ColBERT, 完整BERT): MRR@10 = 34.9%。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]
      - 模型[D] (ColBERT, 5层BERT): MRR@10 未报告具体数值，但用于消融实验。 [evidence-24-d4689256-8cfe-4ccf-b787-8c258fc66fd3]

ABSTRACT
Recent progress in Natural Language Understanding (NLU) is driving fast-paced advances in Information Retrieval (IR), largely owed
to fine-tuning deep language models (LMs) for document ranking.

While remarkably effective, the ranking models based on these LMs
increase computational cost by orders of magnitude over prior approaches, particularly as they must feed each query–document pair
through a massive neural network to compute a single relevance
score.

To tackle this, we present ColBERT, a novel ranking model
that adapts deep LMs (in particular, BERT) for efficient retrieval.

ColBERT introduces a late interaction architecture that independently encodes the query and the document using BERT and then
employs a cheap yet powerful interaction step that models their
fine-grained similarity.

By delaying and yet retaining this finegranular interaction, ColBERT can leverage the expressiveness of
deep LMs while simultaneously gaining the ability to pre-compute
document representations offline, considerably speeding up query
processing.

Beyond reducing the cost of re-ranking the documents
retrieved by a traditional model, ColBERT’s pruning-friendly interaction mechanism enables leveraging vector-similarity indexes
for end-to-end retrieval directly from a large document collection.

We extensively evaluate ColBERT using two recent passage search
datasets.

Under late interaction, q and d are separately

3 COLBERT
ColBERT prescribes a simple framework for balancing the quality
and cost of neural IR, particularly deep language models like BERT.

As introduced earlier, delaying the query–document interaction can
facilitate cheap neural re-ranking (i.e., through pre-computation)
and even support practical end-to-end neural retrieval (i.e., through
pruning via vector-similarity search).

ColBERT addresses how to
do so while still preserving the effectiveness of state-of-the-art
models, which condition the bulk of their computations on the
joint query–document pair.

Even though ColBERT’s late-interaction framework can be applied to a wide variety of architectures (e.g., CNNs, RNNs, transformers, etc.), we choose to focus this work on bi-directional transformerbased encoders (i.e., BERT) owing to their state-of-the-art effectiveness yet very high computational cost.
3.1 Architecture
Figure 3 depicts the general architecture of ColBERT, which comprises: (a) a query encoder f Q , (b) a document encoder f D , and (c)
the late interaction mechanism.

Given a query q and document d ,
f Q encodes q into a bag of fixed-size embeddings E q while f D encodes d into another bag E d .

Crucially, each embeddings in E q and
E d is contextualized based on the other terms in q or d , respectively.

We describe our BERT-based encoders in §3.2.

Using E q and E d , ColBERT computes the relevance score between q and d via late interaction, which we define as a summation
of maximum similarity (MaxSim) operators.

In particular, we find
the maximum cosine similarity of each v ∈ E q with vectors in E d ,
and combine the outputs via summation.

Besides cosine, we also
evaluate squared L2 distance as a measure of vector similarity.

Intuitively, this interaction mechanism softly searches for each query
term t q —in a manner that reflects its context in the query—against
the document’s embeddings, quantifying the strength of the “match”
via the largest similarity score between t q and a document term t d .

Given these term scores, it then estimates the document relevance
by summing the matching evidence across all query terms.

While more sophisticated matching is possible with other choices
such as deep convolution and aention layers (i.e., as in typical
interaction-focused models), a summation of maximum similarity
computations has two distinctive characteristics.

First, it stands
out as a particularly cheap interaction mechanism, as we examine
its FLOPs in §4.2.

Second, and more importantly, it is amenable
to highly-efficient pruning for top- k retrieval, as we evaluate in
§4.3.

This enables using vector-similarity algorithms for skipping
documents without materializing the full interaction matrix or even
considering each document in isolation.

Other cheap choices (e.g.,
a summation of average similarity scores, instead of maximum) are
possible; however, many are less amenable to pruning.

In §4.4, we
conduct an extensive ablation study that empirically verifies the advantage of our MaxSim-based late interaction against alternatives.
3.2 ery & Document Encoders
Prior to late interaction, ColBERT encodes each query or document
into a bag of embeddings, employing BERT-based encoders.

We
share a single BERT model among our query and document encoders but distinguish input sequences that correspond to queries
and documents by prepending a special token [Q] to queries and
another token [D] to documents.

As we discuss later in more detail,
we typically fix m to be much smaller than BERT’s fixed hidden

While ColBERT’s embedding dimension has limited impact on
the efficiency of query encoding, this step is crucial for controlling
the space footprint of documents, as we show in §4.5.

In addition, it
can have a significant impact on query execution time, particularly

In fact, as we show in §4.2, gathering, stacking, and

Finally, the output

The result is that the dot-product of any two embeddings becomes
equivalent to their cosine similarity, falling in the [− 1 , 1 ] range.

3.4 Offline Indexing: Computing & Storing
Document Embeddings
By design, ColBERT isolates almost all of the computations between
queries and documents, largely to enable pre-computing document
representations offline.

At a high level, our indexing procedure is
straight-forward: we proceed over the documents in the collection
in batches, running our document encoder f D on each batch and
storing the output embeddings per document.

Although indexing
a set of documents is an offline process, we incorporate a few
simple optimizations for enhancing the throughput of indexing.

As
we show in §4.5, these optimizations can considerably reduce the
offline cost of indexing.

To begin with, we exploit multiple GPUs, if available, for faster
encoding of batches of documents in parallel.

When batching, we
pad all documents to the maximum length of a document within
the batch. 3 To make capping the sequence length on a per-batch
basis more effective, our indexer proceeds through documents in
groups of B (e.g., B = 100,000) documents.

It sorts these documents
by length and then feeds batches of b (e.g., b = 128) documents of
comparable length through our encoder.

This length-based bucketing is sometimes refered to as a BucketIterator in some libraries
(e.g., allenNLP).

Lastly, while most computations occur on the GPU,
we found that a non-trivial portion of the indexing time is spent on
pre-processing the text sequences, primarily BERT’s WordPiece tokenization.

Exploiting that these operations are independent across
documents in a batch, we parallelize the pre-processing across the
available CPU cores.

Once the document representations are produced, they are saved
to disk using 32-bit or 16-bit values to represent each dimension.

As we describe in §3.5 and 3.6, these representations are either
simply loaded from disk for ranking or are subsequently indexed
for vector-similarity search, respectively.

3.6 End-to-end Top- k Retrieval with ColBERT
As mentioned before, ColBERT’s late-interaction operator is specifically designed to enable end-to-end retrieval from a large collection,
largely to improve recall relative to term-based retrieval approaches.

This section is concerned with cases where the number of documents to be ranked is too large for exhaustive evaluation of each
possible candidate document, particularly when we are only interested in the highest scoring ones.

Concretely, we focus here on
retrieving the top- k results directly from a large document collection with N (e.g., N = 10 , 000 , 000) documents, where k  N .

To do so, we leverage the pruning-friendly nature of the MaxSim
operations at the backbone of late interaction.

In our faiss -based implementation, we use an IVFPQ index (“inverted file with product quantization”).

This index partitions the

For serving queries,

Moreover,
the index conducts the similarity computations in this compressed
domain, leading to cheaper computations and thus faster search.

      - 输入：查询词序列q0, q1, ..., ql。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8] <!-- evidence:evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8 -->
      - 处理：添加特殊标记[Q]和[CLS]，并通过[mask]标记补足到固定长度。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8] <!-- evidence:evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb,evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8 -->
      - 编码：通过共享的BERT模型和线性层生成上下文嵌入。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
      - 输出：经过L2归一化的固定大小的嵌入袋Eq。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be] [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8] <!-- evidence:evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be,evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8 -->
    - 文档编码（离线）
      - 输入：文档词序列d0, d1, ..., dn。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8] <!-- evidence:evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8 -->
      - 处理：添加特殊标记[D]和[CLS]，不加[mask]。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be] <!-- evidence:evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be -->
      - 编码：通过共享的BERT模型和线性层生成上下文嵌入。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
      - 过滤：移除标点符号对应的嵌入。 [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8] <!-- evidence:evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8 -->
      - 输出：经过L2归一化的嵌入袋Ed。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be] <!-- evidence:evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be -->
    - 评分（后期交互）
      - 输入：Eq和Ed。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f -->
      - 计算：对Eq中的每个嵌入，计算其与Ed中所有嵌入的点积（因L2归一化，等价于余弦相似度），取最大值，然后将所有最大值求和。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f,evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089 -->
      - 输出：相关性得分Sq,d。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089] <!-- evidence:evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089 -->
    - 索引（离线）
      - 批量处理文档，使用多GPU、长度分桶、多核预处理等优化。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12] <!-- evidence:evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12 -->
      - 以32-bit或16-bit浮点数将文档嵌入保存到磁盘。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12] <!-- evidence:evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12 -->
      - 可选：构建IVFPQ索引以支持端到端检索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
    - 端到端检索 (两阶段)
      - 第一阶段 (近似检索)：使用IVFPQ索引，对每个查询嵌入搜索邻近单元，合并得到候选文档集K。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - 第二阶段 (精确重排序)：对候选集K使用标准ColBERT重排序步骤。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
  - 算法步骤
    - 训练
      - 使用三元组 (q, d+, d-) 进行训练。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089] <!-- evidence:evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089 -->
      - 损失函数：成对softmax交叉熵损失。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089] <!-- evidence:evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089 -->
      - 优化器：Adam。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089] <!-- evidence:evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089 -->
      - 微调：共享的BERT模型、线性层和特殊标记[Q]、[D]的嵌入。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089] <!-- evidence:evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089 -->
      - 注意：交互机制（MaxSim）本身无可训练参数。 [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089] <!-- evidence:evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089 -->
    - 重排序
      - 使用BM25等模型检索出top-k文档。 [evidence-6-6e1dee63-f411-44ce-b0fe-f4a78524083d] <!-- evidence:evidence-6-6e1dee63-f411-44ce-b0fe-f4a78524083d -->
      - 从磁盘/索引加载这些文档的预计算嵌入。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7] <!-- evidence:evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7 -->
      - 对查询进行实时编码。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7] <!-- evidence:evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7 -->
      - 执行穷举MaxSim计算。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7] <!-- evidence:evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7 -->
      - 按得分排序，输出最终的top-k文档。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7] <!-- evidence:evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7 -->
    - 端到端检索
      - 构建IVFPQ索引。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - 查询阶段1：近似搜索候选文档。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - 查询阶段2：精确重排序候选文档。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
  - 公式/变量
    - 公式(1): Eq = Normalize(CNN(BERT("[Q] q0 q1 ... ql ##... #"))) [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8] <!-- evidence:evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8 -->
      - q0, q1, ..., ql: 查询词序列。
      - ##... #: 用于补足查询到固定长度的[mask]标记。
      - CNN: 用于降维的线性层。
      - Normalize: L2归一化。
      - BERT: 共享的BERT编码器。
    - 公式(2): Ed = Filter(Normalize(CNN(BERT("[D] d0, d1, ..., dn")))) [evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8] <!-- evidence:evidence-14-e1770084-bdf8-48e4-83e3-e64e246070c8 -->
      - d0, d1, ..., dn: 文档词序列。
      - Filter: 移除标点符号嵌入。
    - 公式(3): S_q,d = Σ_{i∈[|Eq|]} max_{j∈[|Ed|]} (Eq_i · Ed^T_j) [evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089] <!-- evidence:evidence-15-4adc342c-5414-4d94-9701-285b33658089 -->
      - S_q,d: 查询q和文档d的相关性得分。
      - |Eq|: 查询嵌入的数量。
      - |Ed|: 文档嵌入的数量。
      - ·: 点积（因归一化，等价于余弦相似度）。
    - 关键变量
      - m: 线性层输出的嵌入维度，远小于BERT的隐藏维度，用于控制存储。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be] <!-- evidence:evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be -->
      - l: 查询的token数量。
      - n: 文档的token数量。
      - max_q: 查询补足后的固定长度。
      - P: IVFPQ索引中聚类中心的数量（默认为2000）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - p: 每个查询嵌入搜索的邻近单元数（默认为10）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - k': 每个查询嵌入在近似检索中返回的嵌入数（默认为1000）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - k: 最终返回的文档数（默认为1000）。
      - s: 每个嵌入被分割的子向量数（默认为16）。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - B: 索引时长度分桶的组大小（默认为100,000）。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12] <!-- evidence:evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12 -->
      - b: 索引时每批处理的文档数（默认为128）。 [evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12] <!-- evidence:evidence-16-c941b7d7-1f56-41ff-8b14-3f85dfda5f12 -->
      - N: 文档集合大小（示例中为10,000,000）。 [evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7] <!-- evidence:evidence-17-b6668f4f-cbcf-445a-822e-bc3b1ac15bd7 -->
  - 模型与组件
    - ColBERT架构
      - 查询编码器 f_Q: 将查询编码为嵌入袋Eq。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f,evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
      - 文档编码器 f_D: 将文档编码为嵌入袋Ed。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f,evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
      - 后期交互机制: 使用MaxSim计算相关性得分。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f -->
    - BERT (基础编码器)
      - 作用：为查询和文档生成上下文感知的嵌入。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f -->
      - 共享：查询和文档编码器共享同一个BERT模型。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
      - 区分：通过不同的特殊标记（[Q]和[D]）来区分输入序列类型。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
    - 线性层 (CNN)
      - 作用：将BERT的输出维度降低到更小的m维度，以控制存储和传输开销。 [evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be] <!-- evidence:evidence-13-da2ae057-9d1a-4daa-9cbd-3f113e0112be -->
    - MaxSim操作
      - 什么是MaxSim: 一个求和的最大相似度操作。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f -->
      - 在方法中的位置：它是后期交互的核心，在查询和文档独立编码后执行。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f -->
      - 与相邻概念的关系：
        - 它替代了传统模型中的全交互矩阵或注意力层。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
        - 它的求和特性比平均相似度更有利，因为强调了词条的最大匹配，且更有利于剪枝。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
    - 嵌入袋 (Bag of Embeddings)
      - 什么是嵌入袋：一个无序的嵌入向量集合，每个向量对应一个token的上下文表示。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f -->
      - 在方法中的位置：查询和文档编码器的输出，作为后期交互的输入。 [evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f] <!-- evidence:evidence-11-412caa52-f1cb-407b-903b-c552813cfd5f -->
    - IVFPQ索引
      - 什么是IVFPQ: 一种基于倒排文件和乘积量化的向量索引，用于大规模近似最近邻搜索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - 在方法中的位置：用于实现ColBERT的端到端检索，在执行MaxSim前先快速筛选候选文档。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
      - 与相邻概念的关系：
        - 它利用了ColBERT的MaxSim操作适合剪枝的特性。 [evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb] <!-- evidence:evidence-12-a9f5aaa8-104e-4675-8788-59b9779936eb -->
        - 它将向量空间划分为多个单元以加速搜索。 [evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084] <!-- evidence:evidence-18-d383a008-a783-4249-a6d8-74482f065084 -->
